subject.title: [Feature Request] Telegram Channel: Support Thread Binding for Subagent Sessions

question: Should Telegram expose native subagent child-topic session spawning now, and should that be done by extending the current core session-binding adapter/capability path while keeping normal Telegram placement as current?
rationale: Current main has binding primitives, but choosing child-topic exposure changes Telegram user-visible topic creation, message routing, session persistence, and plugin capability/API shape.

options.title: Review or replace the active Telegram PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82023 as the main design input, resolve conflicts and review findings, and require final-head live Telegram proof before merge.

options.title: Defer child-topic spawning
options.body: Keep current-conversation Telegram binding only until maintainers settle the visibility/defaults model with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/98918 and the broader policy issues.

options.title: Reject Telegram child-topic subagent spawning
options.body: Close this issue and associated candidate PRs if maintainers decide internal subagent work should not create Telegram topics.

recommendation.title: Review or replace the active Telegram PR
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82023 as the main design input, resolve conflicts and review findings, and require final-head live Telegram proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The current core adapter path and thread-binding policy gates trace most directly to his merged core refactor.
